newsitem.title: USA: Volcker commission to investigate Swiss ombudsman.
newsitem.headline: Volcker commission to investigate Swiss ombudsman.

text.p: A commission headed by prominent U.S. banker Paul Volcker will investigate the methods used by the Swiss banking ombudsman who reported finding only $8,750 clearly belonging to Holocaust victims in Swiss banks, sources close to the probe said on Tuesday.

The investigation into the methodology used by ombudsman Hanspeter Haeni was decided before his announcement on Tuesday that only $8,750 of the $1.3 million uncovered so far in dormant accounts belonged to Jewish victims of the Holocaust.
The announcement stunned and angered Jewish groups.

The sources, close to the accounting firms hired by the Volcker commission for an investigative audit of Swiss banks, said the probe would not only include the ombudsman's methodology but that of the Swiss banking system itself.
They said Haeni sent detailed questionnaires to the banks made out by claimants and left it to the banks themselves to determine if the accounts existed.

To probe charges of a cover-up, Jewish groups and Swiss banks agreed in May to set up an independent panel headed by Volcker, a former U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman, to search for any wealth that escaped two previous sweeps by banks.

Haeni, at a press conference in Zurich, said it was up to the Volcker commission to judge whether the banks were acting in good faith, but added: "I have the impression that the banks are working very well."

The commission will also work with a historical panel due to win parliament's approval next month with a broad mandate to probe Switzerland's wartime role as a financial centre -- a role that has come under fire as thousands of previously secret U.S. documents allege that Switzerland collaborated closely with the Third Reich.
Kalman Sultanik, a vice president of the World Jewish Congress, called Haeni's probe "pathetic" and said he was "acting as a photo copying service for the Swiss banks."

Presenting his first report on a search launched after Swiss banks came under pressure from Jewish groups, Haeni said funds owned by Jewish Holocaust victims made up only a tiny part of the unclaimed wealth Swiss banks have found so far.

Haeni, whose work has been dismissed by Jewish critics as a "cruel hoax" to protect Swiss banks, said his office would continue to act as the central contact point for Holocaust account inquiries for an indefinite period.
Swiss banks deny accusations by Jewish groups and plaintiffs in two class-action suits that they may be sitting on billions of dollars in unclaimed wealth left behind by Hitler's victims.

Haeni said he believed many accounts had already been found in a previous 1960s sweep of Swiss bank vaults and that some accounts still left might yield nothing. He gave the example of one he discovered with now worthless 1930s Romanian bonds.
